verifications.claim: As of April 2, 2026, President Trump has fired Pam Bondi as Attorney General.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Trump fires Attorney General Pam Bondi" (R1); "President Donald Trump is removing Pam Bondi as attorney general" (R2); URLs dated 2026/04/02 across sources
verifications.reasoning: All sources directly confirm Trump fired Bondi as AG around April 2, 2026.

verifications.claim: President Trump has appointed Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche as the acting Attorney General.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche... will serve as acting Attorney General" (R1); "replacing her with Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state Trump appointed Blanche as acting AG.

verifications.claim: Lee Zeldin is the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Lee Zeldin, the administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency" (R1); "EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin" (R4, R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly identify Zeldin as EPA Administrator.

verifications.claim: Lee Zeldin is considered the frontrunner to replace Pam Bondi permanently.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Zeldin remains the heavy favorite on prediction market Kalshi, which sees him with a 55 percent chance... then Lee at 10 percent" (R4); "Lee Zeldin is the overwhelming favorite... 53% chance on Kalshi... 68% on Polymarket" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Prediction markets explicitly position Zeldin as frontrunner for permanent replacement.

verifications.claim: Todd Blanche served as Trump's defense attorney in several criminal cases.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Blanche previously served as Trump's defense attorney in the cases... by Manhattan DA Alvin Bragg and... Jack Smith" (R3); "served as Trump's personal criminal defense attorney" (R4); "served as Trump’s defense attorney across several criminal cases" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm Blanche's role as Trump's defense attorney in multiple cases.

verifications.claim: Todd Blanche will take over leadership of the Department of Justice (DOJ) immediately as acting attorney general.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: "Over the next month I will be working tirelessly to transition the office of Attorney General to... Todd Blanche" (R1, R2); Blanche "will step in to serve as Acting Attorney General" (R3) but with transition period noted
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Blanche as acting AG but specify a one-month transition period by Bondi, contradicting 'immediately'.

verifications.claim: Lee Zeldin has reportedly been in discussions with Trump.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources mention Trump considering Zeldin and a recent meeting on unrelated EPA business (wildfire prevention), but no reports of discussions specifically with Zeldin about the AG role.

verifications.claim: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has been mentioned as a permanent replacement candidate for Pam Bondi.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton" (listed in candidates, R4); "Texas Attorney General... Ken Paxton... drawing bets" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly list Paxton as a mentioned candidate for permanent replacement.

verifications.claim: Sen. Mike Lee (R-Utah) has been mentioned as a permanent replacement candidate for Pam Bondi.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Utah Senator Mike Lee" (listed in candidates, R4); "Sen. Mike Lee (R-Utah)" (drawing bets, R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly list Sen. Mike Lee as a mentioned candidate for permanent replacement.

verifications.claim: Trump was reportedly dissatisfied with Bondi's handling of DOJ files related to Jeffrey Epstein.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Bondi is widely seen as having bungled the release of files related to Epstein" (R1); "backlash... over how she handled the files related to... Jeffrey Epstein" (R2); "criticized Bondi's handling of the DOJ's files... Jeffrey Epstein" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly report Trump's dissatisfaction with Bondi's Epstein files handling.

verifications.claim: Trump was reportedly dissatisfied with Bondi's perceived lack of prosecution of his political opponents.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Trump had become irritated with Bondi for not going after his political opponents enough" (R2); "frustration that the Justice Department isn't doing enough to target his political opponents for prosecution" (R3); "had not investigated or prosecuted enough of his political opponents" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state Trump's dissatisfaction over insufficient prosecutions of opponents.

verifications.claim: Trump announced that Bondi will be transitioning to a position in the private sector.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "she will be transitioning to a much needed and important new job in the private sector" (R1, R2, R3, R7)
verifications.reasoning: Trump's announcement directly quoted across sources states Bondi transitioning to private sector.

verifications.claim: Bondi's departure follows increased pressure from Congress regarding her management of the DOJ.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Subpoena for April 14 deposition on Epstein files (DOJ handling); hearings and pressure noted before April 2 firing (R1, R2, R3); "Bondi's departure follows... pressure from Congress" temporally linked
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm congressional pressure (subpoenas, hearings) on DOJ/Epstein management preceding and noted around her ouster.
